notes: Urban green roofs have potential for local urban climate change mitigation, as they have been demonstrated to uptake CO2 from the atmosphere. However, most roofs are too small to qualify for area-integrating direct surface-atmosphere exchange measurements using the eddy covariance technique (EC), resulting in sparse data on net CO2 sequestration capacities. Small scale methods such as leaf chamber or automated surface chambers (AC) may provide a monitoring alternative for smaller roofs. To assess whether alternative methods can produce representative data on the CO2 sequestration capacity of an extensive green roof, simultaneous measurements at the scale of leaf, plants, and roof were conducted. The software provided includes the comparison of eddy covariance, automated chamber, and leaf chamber data with the respective code to replicate the images of the research article "Representativity of CO2 exchange on extensive green roofs: scaling from leaf to plant, and plant to roof scale".
